author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Upper Valley Haven is preparing to open a 20-bed, year-round emergency shelter and daytime resource center in White River Junction, expanding services for people across the New Hampshire-Vermont border region. The Patrick and Marcelle Leahy Shelter and Resource Center at 608 North Main Street is expected to welcome its first guests in the coming weeks.

The facility replaces a seasonal shelter in Lebanon, New Hampshire, that offered 14 beds for roughly three months each winter. That building is slated for demolition as part of a roundabout project. During its most recent season, 66 people stayed for a combined total of about 100 nights, while an average of two people per night were turned away because space was unavailable.

The Haven raised $10.2 million for the new center and expects it to provide about 5,000 overnight stays annually for roughly 100 people. Year-round operation is intended to reduce weather-driven gaps and connect guests with support during daytime hours. For New Hampshire communities in the Upper Valley, the opening adds nearby capacity as local providers contend with persistent housing insecurity and limited emergency beds.
dek: The 20-bed center in White River Junction will replace a smaller seasonal Lebanon shelter and serve the broader cross-border region.
headline: Upper Valley Haven readies year-round shelter serving New Hampshire region
location: Upper Valley, New Hampshire and Vermont
